$comment: Schedule task permission policy (Testing #79042): the expected allow / deny answer of every actor and operation, as rules over actor attributes and two settings. The Java helper matrix (SchedulePermissionHelperMatrixTest) and the e2e entry-point matrix (stylebi-enterprise e2e/tests/api/schedule/permission-matrix) both read this file. The rules are the ones agreed on 2026-10-30 (stylebi-enterprise e2e/tests/api/schedule/permission-matrix/RULES-TO-DECIDE.md). An expression uses the attributes, the settings share (schedule.options.shareTaskInGroup) and deleteOnlyByOwner (schedule.options.deleteTaskOnlyByOwner, "Modify By Owner Only" in the UI), other rule ids, true / false, and && || ! ( ). Every refused request must answer an error and change nothing.

attributes.orgAdmin: organization administrator of the task's org
attributes.shareMember: in a group with the owner
attributes.grantHolder: explicit SCHEDULE_TASK READ+WRITE+DELETE on the task, from the EM Content > Repository editor that Bug #79853 removes; it grants nothing

rules.expr: siteAdmin || sameOrg && (orgAdmin || owner || ownerAdmin || share && shareMember)
rules.basis: RepletEngine.hasTaskPermission ("may see") without the explicit grant (A1)
rules.changes: #79853: the EM list and removeScheduleTask still accept an explicit grant

rules.basis: ScheduleTaskService.canDeleteTask: "Modify By Owner Only" stops group members from every change, opening the task included (A2, A4)

rules.changes: #79865: the public API refuses group members and its stop skips SCHEDULER; #79866: EM list / run / stop skip SCHEDULER
#79865: the public API refuses group members and ignores deleteOnlyByOwner; #79866: EM delete skips SCHEDULER; #79864: the public API delete doesn't check dependent tasks

rules.basis: the Portal task list shows only the user's own and the group's tasks (A6)
ScheduleTaskIdentityChecker.isOwnerAllowed for the task owner: the owner itself or an admin of it (C1, C2)
ScheduleTaskService.checkTaskIdentityPermission, the actor makes itself the owner: it must administer the current owner (C3)
rules.changes: #79863: any caller may make itself the owner

rules.basis: checkSaveRefusals with a sheet / target every user of the org may read: only the owner organization of the task refuses (B1, B2)

checkSaveRefusals with the owner's private sheet: the run principal (the owner) may read it, the saver must too, through the check that lets the sheet's owner and its administrators read it; a site admin saver isn't checked (B2)
ScheduleTaskIdentityChecker.isOwnerAllowed: the task owner may be named only by itself or an admin of it; an import that overwrites the task names its owner (C1)
ScheduleTaskService.checkTaskIdentityPermission: admin of the current and the new owner (C3)
rules.changes: #79863: a group member may make itself the owner

rules.basis: internal-task targets and imports (#77531, B3, C2), folder grants a site admin always has
import may name another user of the org as owner only for an admin of that user; an owner of another org is moved to the importer's org first (C2)
checkSaveRefusals: the run principal (the execute-as identity, or the owner) may not read the sheet / query / target, so even a site admin's save is refused (B2, B3)
